knowledge_point.title: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=8 \\ 2x+6y &=16.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 6 & 16\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 6 & 16\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3y &=8 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+3y=8.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=8-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=8-3y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}8-3y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-1 \\ -3x+6y &=3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -3 & 6 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -3 & 6 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-1 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=-1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2y-1,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2y-1 \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2y-1 \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=-2 \\ -4x+24y &=11.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & -2 \\ -4 & 24 & 11\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & -2 \\ -4 & 24 & 11\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -6 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-6y &=-2 \\ 0x+0y &=3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=3$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=3,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+7y &=-2 \\ 6x+42y &=-13.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 6 & 42 & -13\end{array}\right]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 6 & 42 & -13\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & \sim\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 7 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+7y &=-2 \\ 0x+0y &=-1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-1$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-1,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.
